text:
### Observed differences

- The six activities between A30 and A31 changed from partly optional to near-universal. Earlier, A33, A35 and A36 each ran in about 49 in 100 traces and A37, A38 and A39 each in about 52 in 100; in the later window each of them runs in about 98–100 in 100 traces. [POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008, POS009, POS010]
- The two groups also changed from alternatives to jointly executed blocks. Earlier, an activity of the first group (A33, A35, A36) and one of the second (A37, A38, A39) shared a trace in only about 1–2 in 100 cases; in the later window they share it in about 98 in 100, with the first group before the second in about 95–98 in 100. Order inside each group stays unfixed in both windows (each internal pair appears in both orders in similar shares). [REL039, REL045, REL047, REL050, REL037, REL044, REL055, REL059]
- Routing follows the same pattern. Earlier, A30's outgoing transitions spread evenly over all six group activities (about 14–18 in 100 each); in the later window A30 leads almost only to A35, A33 and A36 (about 36, 31 and 29 in 100) and to A37, A38 or A39 in about 1 in 100 or less. Earlier, roughly three in ten outgoing transitions of A33, A35 and A36 went to A31; in the later window they lead to A37, A38 and A39 instead (about 7–13 in 100 each) and to A31 in about 1 in 100 or less. [DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008]
- The path from A30 to A31 became longer: earlier, A31 followed A30 within five steps in about 199 in 200 traces (usually four steps apart); in the later window this holds in only about 5 in 200 traces, and gaps from A30, A33, A35 or A36 to the second-group activities and to A31 now sit mostly at four to five steps. A30 now sits slightly earlier (mean position about 0.67 to 0.62) and A31 slightly later (about 0.80 to 0.82). [LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008, LAG011, LAG013, POS003, POS004]
- A04 became rare and moved later: it ran in about 59 in 100 traces earlier and about 26 in 100 in the later window, with its mean position moving from about 0.20 to 0.38. Earlier, about 90 in 100 of A04's outgoing transitions went to A15, and A14 led to A04 in about 57 in 100 of its outgoing transitions; in the later window A15 takes about 40 in 100 of A04's outgoing transitions (the rest spread thinly over many activities), A14 leads to A04 in only about 12 in 100 and to A15 in about 79 in 100. [POS001, DIR002, DIR004, REL001, REL002, LAG001, LAG002]
- Smaller redistributions: the outgoing transitions of A02 and A10 now spread across many new successors (small bases: A02 seen in 12 before vs 40 after traces, A10 in 11 vs 50), and A15's execution relative to the six-activity block became less strictly ordered (interleaved or repeated in about 4 in 10 traces, up from about 2 in 10). [DIR001, DIR003, REL019, REL020, REL021]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the two activity groups between A30 and A31 stopped being alternatives: earlier, each trace executed one of the two groups (about 50/50, with cross-group traces at about 1–2 in 100), while in the later window nearly every trace executes both groups in sequence — A30 feeds the first group (A33, A35, A36), the first group feeds the second (A37, A38, A39), and A31 now follows the whole block rather than the first group directly. This is shown directly by the relation indicators (cross-group co-occurrence rising to about 98 in 100 with a consistent first-before-second order), corroborated by the redirection of A30's and of A33/A35/A36's outgoing transitions, by the participation jump of all six activities, and by the near-disappearance of A30→A31 within five steps. The many relation items describe one underlying trace behaviour and are not independent confirmations; still, 99 items qualified against roughly 1 expected for an unchanged process, so chance sampling cannot explain the pattern as a whole. Limitations: the order inside each group remains unfixed, so the hypothesis covers the group sequence, not a strict order within groups; and the evidence cannot rule out that both behaviour patterns already existed as variants and only their mix shifted between the windows — the earlier window shows the alternative pattern at about 50/50, so a "both groups" variant, if it existed then, was rare. [REL039, REL045, REL050, DIR005, DIR006, LAG004, POS005, POS008]

Other differences: A04's participation fell from about 59 to about 26 in 100 traces and its position moved later, with A14 now usually leading directly to A15; this is consistent with A04 becoming skippable in most traces, but the evidence does not show what, if anything, takes its place in the cases where it no longer appears. The outgoing transitions of A02 and A10 also redistributed across many successors, though on small observation bases. [POS001, DIR002, DIR004, DIR001, DIR003]
